title: Areas Related to Circles
notes: Sector = region between two radii and the arc they cut off. Minor sector < 180 deg worth of angle, major sector = 360 - minor angle.
Segment = region between a chord and the arc. Minor segment is the smaller piece, major segment is the rest of the circle.
Area of segment = Area of sector - Area of the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord. This is THE key formula for every segment problem.
For angle 90 or 60 or 120 degrees, the triangle part is often a standard triangle (right isosceles, equilateral) so its area can be computed directly instead of using general trig.
Unless stated otherwise, use pi = 22/7 in NCERT problems (some problems explicitly say use pi=3.14 -- always check what's specified).
Real-life sector problems (grazing horse, umbrella ribs, wiper blades, brooch design) are just repeated applications of arc length and sector area formulas -- identify r and theta, then plug in.

formulas.name: Arc Length
formulas.use: Length of the curved part of a sector.

formulas.name: Area of Segment
formulas.formula: Area of sector - Area of triangle (formed by the 2 radii + chord)

formulas.name: Area of full circle
formulas.use: Base formula; sector formula is a fraction of this.

examples.question: Find area of segment AYB in a circle where sector area is 462 sq cm and triangle OAB area is (441/4)root3 sq cm.
examples.solution: Area of segment = Area of sector - Area of triangle = 462 - (441/4)root3 = (21/4)(88 - 21root3) sq cm.
